extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and creative writing students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on using Freytag's five-act (pyramid) dramatic structure to shape short stories and other narratives, with implied quality criteria for pacing, escalation, climax, and resolution. Useful for authors evaluating story structure or planning drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 1: Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes setting (time/place/atmosphere); Introduces main characters; Inciting incident ("exciting force") suggests the primary conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up the world and stakes; the inciting incident should appear early enough to grab the reader. Avoid long, aimless background that delays the exciting force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 2: Rising Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict escalates as the protagonist pursues a goal; Series of complications, each raising stakes; Tension increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure escalation rather than repetition — each complication should meaningfully raise stakes or complicate the protagonist's path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 3: Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: The story's turning point (highest point of the pyramid); Protagonist's fate is sealed (success in comedy, downfall in tragedy); Single moment of greatest intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The climax should be the single moment of greatest intensity and the logical outcome of prior events; it must feel earned by the rising action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 4: Falling Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Consequences of the climax play out; "Final suspense" — possibility of an unexpected outcome; Movement toward resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain narrative tension during the fallout; avoid rushing to resolution or flattening remaining stakes too quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act 5: Resolution / Denouement / Catastrophe
rubrics_metrics.description: Loose ends tied; New equilibrium (happy in comedy; "catastrophe" — often deaths — in tragedy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a satisfying new equilibrium without truncating or over-extending the denouement; resolve major threads while respecting tone (comic vs tragic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Each act must have a clear function
rubrics_metrics.description: Each act has clear function — no narrative drag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scenes or sections that don't serve an act's purpose; every scene should advance exposition, escalation, climax, falling action, or resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rising action must genuinely escalate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series of complications should increase stakes, pressure, or cost; repeated or flat obstacles indicate weak pacing or structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax must be earned
rubrics_metrics.description: Climax is 'earned' by everything before it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The turning point should be the logical culmination of setup and escalation; avoid deus ex machina or climaxes that contradict earlier development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denouement pacing should be appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance tying up loose ends with preserving momentum; too-short denouements feel rushed, too-long ones dilute impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inciting incident timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Inciting incident appears early enough to grab the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the exciting force sufficiently early to establish the primary conflict and propel rising action; don't bury it in excessive exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Falling action should maintain tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Falling action maintains tension despite movement toward conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even as events move toward resolution, keep 'final suspense' alive — allow for an unexpected outcome or lingering stakes until resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variant structures (use/fit as alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants: Three-Act (Setup / Confrontation / Resolution); Four-Act (Setup / Conflict / Crisis / Resolution); Seven-Point Story Structure (Hook / Plot Turn 1 / Pinch 1 / Midpoint / Pinch 2 / Plot Turn 2 / Resolution); Fichtean Curve (multiple rising-action mini-crises before the climax; no exposition; in medias res).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These alternative structures adapt Freytag's principles to different pacing and storytelling needs — choose a variant when its shape better fits your story's demands (e.g., Fichtean Curve for in medias res openings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Freytag's Pyramid as an evaluative standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The classic shape of dramatic narrative — and the implicit standard against which most short stories' structural quality is judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pyramid as a diagnostic tool: check whether each act fulfills its role, whether escalation and payoff align, and whether the overall arc reads as coherent and purposeful.
